scope.purpose: Research-backed evidence_sources and free_task_specific_learning_resources for one disjoint area-item batch.

evidence_sources.title: Learning Materials: Introduction and Ethics; computational social science curriculum
evidence_sources.publisher: Summer Institutes in Computational Social Science
evidence_sources.locator: Day 1 Introduction and Ethics; curriculum overview and linked lectures, slides, code and exercises.
evidence_sources.what_supported: Computational social science combines a social-science question with suitable computational data and methods; ethics is part of the workflow.
evidence_sources.limitations: Teaching materials assume basic working R knowledge; a curriculum does not validate a particular construct, dataset or inference.
evidence_sources.cost_access: Open teaching materials; no charge to view/download. Computing setup may be needed for exercises.

evidence_sources.title: Understanding Society with Big Data: Computational Social Science
evidence_sources.publisher: University of Edinburgh, School of Informatics and School of Political and Social Science
evidence_sources.locator: Learning outcomes and course outline: formulate questions about social phenomena, select computational methods, and account for ethics and bias.
evidence_sources.what_supported: Question formulation precedes method selection and requires social interpretation and limitation awareness.
evidence_sources.limitations: Course page states all rights reserved; page describes course/labs but does not grant an open licence or prove unrestricted reuse.
evidence_sources.cost_access: Page and materials are freely viewable; no course price stated on this page. No credential or reuse rights inferred.

free_task_specific_learning_resources.title: Action for Computational Thinking in Social Sciences: open course materials
free_task_specific_learning_resources.publisher: ACTiSS project; University of Warsaw, University of Groningen and Alexander von Humboldt Institute for Internet and Society
free_task_specific_learning_resources.locator: Course modules, curricula, exercises and discussion questions; computational modelling and social-network analysis modules; freely available materials for learners and teachers.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.what_supported: Free structured computational-social-science learning that starts from social processes and connects them to computational methods.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.limitations: Broad course modules; the learner must still define and justify an item-specific social research question and its data.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.cost_access: Materials explicitly described as freely available. Live FutureLearn course access may have separate platform terms; downloadable materials avoid relying on a paid certificate.

evidence_sources.title: Research Ethics and New Forms of Data for Social and Economic Research
evidence_sources.publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
evidence_sources.locator: Report overview and guidance on ethical approaches to new forms of data in social and economic research.
evidence_sources.what_supported: New and digital data require explicit ethical consideration alongside access and analytic use.
evidence_sources.limitations: Policy paper, not binding law, a technical provenance standard or a substitute for local ethics review.
evidence_sources.cost_access: Report page freely accessible; no charge identified.

evidence_sources.title: Foundations of research data management
evidence_sources.locator: Sections on data lifecycle, documentation, responsible sharing, legal and ethical responsibilities, and managing data during a project.
evidence_sources.what_supported: Provenance, documentation, responsible access, preservation and ethical stewardship are connected research-data practices.
evidence_sources.limitations: UK-focused service guidance; does not state Nigerian legal requirements. Follow current Nigerian law and institutional review requirements for local work.
evidence_sources.cost_access: Learning pages freely accessible; no fee stated.

free_task_specific_learning_resources.title: Data skills modules
free_task_specific_learning_resources.locator: Interactive modules: Sourcing data ethically; Ethical consent and data sharing; de-identification/anonymisation of transcript and quantitative data; documenting data collections.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.what_supported: Concrete self-paced exercises for ethical sourcing, consent, de-identification and research-data documentation.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.limitations: Examples and policy context are UK-oriented; anonymisation is not a guarantee against re-identification and is not legal advice for Nigeria.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.cost_access: Described as free, interactive, self-paced modules; requires web access.

evidence_sources.title: Best practices for documenting social sciences research data
evidence_sources.locator: Guide sections on documenting social-science data, metadata and decisions for reuse.
evidence_sources.what_supported: Data preparation should leave a comprehensible record of variables, transformations and documentation for later interpretation/reuse.
evidence_sources.limitations: Guidance is not a cleaning algorithm or proof that a cleaned dataset is valid; local governance and study design still control.
evidence_sources.cost_access: PDF freely accessible; no charge identified.

evidence_sources.title: Getting started tutorials
evidence_sources.locator: Tutorials on reading/writing, selecting, deriving columns, summaries, reshaping, combining tables and text data.
evidence_sources.what_supported: Reproducible scripted operations for tabular data transformation and quality inspection.
evidence_sources.limitations: Tool documentation does not determine whether a transformation is substantively justified, ethical or inferentially sound.
evidence_sources.cost_access: Documentation and pandas are free/open source; local computing is required for full exercises.

free_task_specific_learning_resources.title: Data Analysis and Visualization with Python for Social Scientists (alpha)
free_task_specific_learning_resources.locator: Episodes 5–12: file processing, CSV/JSON, pandas reading, row/column selection, aggregation, joins and wide/long formats; learner view uses SAFI and survey datasets.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.what_supported: Hands-on social-science data workflow using Python, Jupyter and pandas, including concrete table preparation tasks.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.limitations: The lesson labels itself alpha; its examples do not teach research design or statistical inference and use non-Nigerian teaching data.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.cost_access: Lesson and datasets freely accessible; Python and packages are free. Installation or an instructor/workshop may be needed.

free_task_specific_learning_resources.title: Best practices for documenting social sciences research data
free_task_specific_learning_resources.locator: Guide sections on documenting data and recording decisions for responsible reuse.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.what_supported: Provides a companion method for recording cleaning decisions and dataset meaning.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.limitations: UK-oriented documentation guidance; it does not teach pandas syntax or certify data quality.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.cost_access: PDF freely accessible; no charge identified.

evidence_sources.title: The Python Tutorial
evidence_sources.locator: Tutorial sections on data structures, modules, input/output, errors and exceptions, and virtual environments/packages.
evidence_sources.what_supported: Python language and environment skills can implement a repeatable computational workflow.
evidence_sources.limitations: General programming instruction does not establish social-research competence, method selection or valid interpretation.
evidence_sources.cost_access: Official tutorial freely accessible; Python is free/open source. Device and internet may be needed.

free_task_specific_learning_resources.title: Data Analysis and Visualization with Python for Social Scientists (alpha)
free_task_specific_learning_resources.locator: Summary and Setup plus episodes 1–12: Python basics, reusable code, CSV/JSON, pandas tables, aggregation, joining and reshaping, with social-science teaching datasets.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.what_supported: A free, hands-on Python path tied specifically to social-science data handling, rather than generic language overview alone.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.limitations: Explicit alpha status; lesson assumes a working Python setup and does not teach theory, sampling or inference.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.cost_access: Materials are freely accessible; Python, Jupyter and listed libraries are free. Computer/internet and setup time are practical costs.

evidence_sources.title: What is R?
evidence_sources.locator: About R: statistical computing and graphics environment and extensible packages.
evidence_sources.what_supported: R is a plausible implementation route for statistical computing and graphics in social-data workflows.
evidence_sources.limitations: The language's capabilities do not select a valid research design, representativeness or interpretation.
evidence_sources.cost_access: R and the R Project pages are free/open source; computer and internet access may be required.

free_task_specific_learning_resources.title: R for Social Scientists
free_task_specific_learning_resources.locator: Summary and Setup and linked lessons: R basics, importing SAFI survey data, data frames/factors, row and column operations, summaries, data wrangling and visualisation.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.what_supported: A hands-on R path expressly designed for social-science data, from import through preparation, summaries and plots.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.limitations: Examples use SAFI teaching data and do not cover all statistical methods or Nigerian contexts; requires installing R and RStudio.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.cost_access: Lesson, R and RStudio are free; no course fee stated. Computer/internet access and setup are practical costs.

evidence_sources.title: What is Jupyter?
evidence_sources.locator: Notebook description: code, narrative text, data and visualisations in one shareable computational document.
evidence_sources.what_supported: A notebook can make computational steps and explanatory narrative inspectable together.
evidence_sources.limitations: A notebook alone does not pin dependencies, guarantee reruns, validate methods or protect sensitive data.
evidence_sources.cost_access: Jupyter is free/open source; local installation needs a computer. Sharing can expose data if permissions are not checked.

evidence_sources.title: The Binder Project
evidence_sources.locator: Uses and guiding principles: linkable interactive environments for teaching and reproducible scientific analysis; public mybinder.org deployment.
evidence_sources.what_supported: Environment specifications can accompany code for a sharable, runnable computational environment.
evidence_sources.limitations: A public hosted session is temporary and resource-limited; public repositories/environments are not appropriate for restricted data. Reproducibility still depends on pinned, available inputs and dependencies.
evidence_sources.cost_access: Binder and mybinder.org public service described as free; no uptime/resource guarantee inferred. Local compute/internet costs may apply.

free_task_specific_learning_resources.title: Binder tutorials
free_task_specific_learning_resources.locator: Get started with Binder; prepare/customize an environment; share computational work and course content; pin dependencies and use Dockerfiles for reproducibility.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.what_supported: Step-by-step setup and reproducibility instruction for a shareable Jupyter execution environment.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.limitations: Technical environment training, not a research-method lesson; public Binder is temporary and not suitable for confidential data.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.cost_access: Tutorials and the community mybinder.org service are free; execution uses community capacity and internet.

evidence_sources.title: Getting started tutorials
evidence_sources.locator: Official sequence covers data types, reading/writing tables, subsetting, derived columns, plots, summaries, reshaping, joining, time series and text.
evidence_sources.what_supported: pandas is a tool for tabular data operations central to many social-data workflows.
evidence_sources.limitations: A pandas operation does not establish measurement validity, sampling adequacy, ethics or causal inference.
evidence_sources.cost_access: pandas and its documentation are free/open source; local Python execution requires a computer.

free_task_specific_learning_resources.title: Data Analysis and Visualization with Python for Social Scientists (alpha)
free_task_specific_learning_resources.locator: Episodes 8–12: read data with pandas, select rows/columns, aggregate, join DataFrames and reshape wide/long social-science tables.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.what_supported: Task-specific practice of pandas operations on social-science teaching data.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.limitations: Alpha lesson; its exercises do not teach when a transformation is conceptually defensible, inference or ethical handling.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.cost_access: Materials and dependencies are free; requires Python setup and computer/internet access.

free_task_specific_learning_resources.title: Getting started tutorials
free_task_specific_learning_resources.locator: Sections on reading/writing, selecting, derived columns, summaries, reshape and combining tables.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.what_supported: Official reference with runnable introductory steps for table preparation and joins.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.limitations: Generic technical examples; learners need a substantive social-data exercise and a documented cleaning rationale.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.cost_access: Free documentation and open-source library; local compute required.

evidence_sources.title: Linear regression diagnostics; Regression diagnostics
evidence_sources.locator: Runnable example with OLS output, residual/QQ/scale-location/leverage diagnostics, VIF and discussion of failure modes; companion regression diagnostics notebook.
evidence_sources.what_supported: A model report should include interpretable estimates and inspect assumptions/influence rather than present coefficients alone.
evidence_sources.limitations: Python examples are implementation instruction; diagnosis is not a guarantee of model correctness, construct validity or causality. Some rules of thumb on the page require judgment.
evidence_sources.cost_access: Documentation and statsmodels are free/open source; compute needed to run notebooks.

evidence_sources.title: Data Analysis for Social Scientists (14.310x, Spring 2023)
evidence_sources.locator: Course description and available lecture/assignment materials on statistics, regression/econometrics, experiments, R and empirical social-science analysis.
evidence_sources.what_supported: Social-science statistical model choice and interpretation are learned within design and empirical reasoning.
evidence_sources.limitations: Advanced quantitative prerequisites; course examples are not Nigerian data and completing OCW materials is not a credential.
evidence_sources.cost_access: OCW materials free to access; no certificate or instructor support implied.

free_task_specific_learning_resources.title: Data Analysis for Social Scientists (14.310x, Spring 2023)
free_task_specific_learning_resources.locator: Lecture notes, problem sets and course materials for probability/statistics, regression/econometrics, research design and applied social-science analysis.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.what_supported: Free structured social-science analysis learning that contextualizes models in questions, designs and evidence.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.limitations: Requires substantial math/statistics preparation; materials are from a 2023 course and examples are not locally tailored.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.cost_access: Materials free; no charge for self-study. No graded certificate or personal instructor access represented.

free_task_specific_learning_resources.title: Linear regression diagnostics
free_task_specific_learning_resources.locator: Notebook example: estimate OLS, inspect diagnostic plots, leverage and VIF; linked discussion explains nonlinearity, autocorrelation, heteroskedasticity and influence.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.what_supported: Practical model-diagnostic exercise that supports transparent interpretation of an applied regression.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.limitations: One linear-model example and dataset; not a general statistics course or evidence that the model answers a causal question.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.cost_access: Free documentation and software; running requires Python environment.

evidence_sources.title: Introduction to digital trace data: Quality, ethics, and analysis
evidence_sources.locator: Course overview and 2026/27 schedule; course focus on how behavioral data are collected, analysed and interpreted, with quality, ethics and inequality; linked lectures, labs and solutions.
evidence_sources.what_supported: Digital trace research involves source/collection choices, quality, interpretation and ethical limitations; platform traces are not self-explanatory measures of populations.
evidence_sources.limitations: The associated Utrecht enrolled course is fee-based for external students (listed at €1,456 in the university course catalogue); the public site exposes some materials but does not establish that all course instruction is open-access.
evidence_sources.cost_access: Public pages/materials appear accessible without payment; full course enrollment is listed at €1,456. Not treated as a free course.

evidence_sources.title: Learning Materials: Collecting Digital Trace Data
evidence_sources.publisher: Summer Institutes in Computational Social Science
evidence_sources.locator: Day 2: Collecting Digital Trace Data and linked lectures, slides, code and exercises.
evidence_sources.what_supported: A computational-social-science teaching unit specifically addresses digital trace collection.
evidence_sources.limitations: Materials assume basic R; do not establish that a particular platform sample is representative or lawful to collect.
evidence_sources.cost_access: Open materials free to access/download; internet and software setup may be required.

free_task_specific_learning_resources.title: Learning Materials: Collecting Digital Trace Data
free_task_specific_learning_resources.publisher: Summer Institutes in Computational Social Science
free_task_specific_learning_resources.locator: Day 2: Collecting Digital Trace Data; linked lecture, slides, code and exercises.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.what_supported: Free structured instruction to examine digital-trace collection choices as a research task.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.limitations: Requires basic R for much of the curriculum; learners must separately establish construct validity, platform terms, ethical permission and sampling limits for their own case.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.cost_access: Materials are open source/free; no course fee for self-study of materials. Data/API access may have separate costs or restrictions.

evidence_sources.title: Quanteda tutorials
evidence_sources.publisher: quanteda project; Kohei Watanabe and Stefan Müller
evidence_sources.locator: Step-by-step chapters for corpus construction, tokens, document-feature matrices, text scaling and document classification including Naive Bayes and topic models.
evidence_sources.what_supported: Computational text analysis includes explicit choices in corpus preparation, tokenisation, feature representation and classification.
evidence_sources.limitations: Tutorials demonstrate methods/software; they do not validate a codebook, language/domain transfer or human meaning. Local language and dialect performance needs its own testing.
evidence_sources.cost_access: Tutorials and R package are free/open source; local R environment required for exercises.

evidence_sources.title: Learning Materials: Text as Data
evidence_sources.publisher: Summer Institutes in Computational Social Science
evidence_sources.locator: Curriculum's text-analysis material and linked teaching resources, alongside introductory ethics and computational social science.
evidence_sources.what_supported: Text-as-data is a specialist computational social-science method, situated within ethics and research questions.
evidence_sources.limitations: Materials assume basic R; they do not show that automated labels equal validated social constructs.
evidence_sources.cost_access: Open teaching materials free; computing and data access may have costs/restrictions.

free_task_specific_learning_resources.title: Quanteda tutorials: quantitative text analysis using R
free_task_specific_learning_resources.publisher: quanteda project; Kohei Watanabe and Stefan Müller
free_task_specific_learning_resources.locator: Chapters for importing text, corpus and tokens, document-feature matrices, text scaling, Naive Bayes classification and topic models.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.what_supported: Free practical sequence from text data to classification with runnable R examples.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.limitations: Tutorial covers computational implementation, not research ethics, annotation validity, construct operationalisation or Nigerian language evaluation.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.cost_access: Free website/software; requires R and internet for first access.

evidence_sources.title: Social Network Analysis: The Networks Connecting People
evidence_sources.publisher: ACTiSS project; University of Warsaw and University of Groningen
evidence_sources.locator: Social Network Analysis course section: three-week module description, course videos, curriculum, models and exercises on network formation and information diffusion.
evidence_sources.what_supported: Social network analysis studies relational structure and processes such as diffusion; method choice depends on a defined relation and network boundary.
evidence_sources.limitations: Course examples do not establish that available edges are complete, meaningful or causal; project page links a FutureLearn option with potentially separate access terms.
evidence_sources.cost_access: Project states teaching materials are freely available; linked platform's enrollment/certificate pricing may vary and is not counted as free here.

evidence_sources.title: Tutorial
evidence_sources.locator: Creating graphs, nodes/edges, graph types, attributes, importing, analysis functions and graph algorithms.
evidence_sources.what_supported: Network representation choices and graph measures are concrete computational operations within network analysis.
evidence_sources.limitations: Library guide is not a social-network research-design course; algorithm output is conditional on graph construction and does not prove causal or social meaning.
evidence_sources.cost_access: Free/open-source documentation and software; local Python setup needed.

free_task_specific_learning_resources.title: Social Network Analysis: The Networks Connecting People
free_task_specific_learning_resources.publisher: ACTiSS project; University of Warsaw, University of Groningen and Alexander von Humboldt Institute for Internet and Society
free_task_specific_learning_resources.locator: Course videos and downloadable curriculum/exercises for the three-week social-network analysis module.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.what_supported: Free social-science-oriented learning on network formation and diffusion, with conceptual framing and exercises.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.limitations: The free materials may be less interactive than the FutureLearn course; it does not decide the learner's network boundary, tie definition or data quality.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.cost_access: ACTiSS says its digital teaching materials are freely available; FutureLearn participation/certificate may have changing terms.

free_task_specific_learning_resources.title: NetworkX Tutorial
free_task_specific_learning_resources.locator: Hands-on sections create graph objects, add node/edge attributes, import data and run graph analysis functions.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.what_supported: Runnable free technical practice that can implement a specified network-analysis task.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.limitations: Not substantive social-science instruction; use only after the tie, unit, boundary and data-generation process are defined.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.cost_access: Free/open source; local Python computing required.

evidence_sources.title: Tutorial
evidence_sources.locator: Official graph creation, graph types, attributes, graph analysis and algorithms walkthrough.
evidence_sources.what_supported: NetworkX offers a code-based route for graph construction, network measures and importing/exporting graph data.
evidence_sources.limitations: Technical capability is not proof that a graph or a particular metric fits a social question.
evidence_sources.cost_access: Free/open source software and docs; requires Python and local compute.

evidence_sources.title: Gephi Quickstart: Visualize and Analyze Your First Network
evidence_sources.locator: Quickstart steps using sample Les Misérables network; import, layout, filtering and basic network statistics/histogram.
evidence_sources.what_supported: Gephi provides an interactive GUI route for exploring and visualising an imported network and inspecting basic measures.
evidence_sources.limitations: Visual layout can mislead; visualization does not validate edge meaning or support causal claims. Sample is literary, not social-research evidence.
evidence_sources.cost_access: Gephi is free/open-source; requires compatible computer and installation.

free_task_specific_learning_resources.title: NetworkX Tutorial
free_task_specific_learning_resources.locator: Official hands-on sequence for creating a graph, defining nodes and edges, attributes, importing and analyzing graphs.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.what_supported: Free practice with coded network construction and analysis for a learner who selects a valid social-network task.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.limitations: Requires Python familiarity; not a method-selection or social-theory lesson.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.cost_access: Free/open source; local software environment and compute required.

free_task_specific_learning_resources.title: Gephi Quickstart
free_task_specific_learning_resources.locator: Follow the first sample network from import through layout and basic statistics; linked downloadable sample file.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.what_supported: Direct free beginner practice for importing, exploring and visually inspecting a network in Gephi.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.limitations: The built-in sample is not a social-science study; visualization choices are not evidence of network quality or social importance.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.cost_access: Free software, tutorial and sample; computer installation required.

evidence_sources.title: Creating Your First Model: The Boltzmann Wealth Model
evidence_sources.locator: First-model notebook progressively implements agents, model steps, data collection and visualisation; model assumptions are listed explicitly.
evidence_sources.what_supported: Agent-based simulation implements explicit individual-agent rules and interaction to inspect emergent model outcomes.
evidence_sources.limitations: The tutorial's toy economic model and its outputs are not evidence about actual populations; results depend on assumptions, parameters and validation.
evidence_sources.cost_access: Mesa, tutorial and sample code are free/open source; Python environment/computing needed. Optional Colab execution depends on third-party service access.

evidence_sources.title: Computational Social Science learning materials
evidence_sources.publisher: Summer Institutes in Computational Social Science
evidence_sources.locator: Course curriculum links lectures, slides, code and exercises in computational social science, including method and ethics foundations.
evidence_sources.what_supported: Simulation is a computational social-science approach to be framed by assumptions and research aims.
evidence_sources.limitations: Materials assume basic R in parts; no simulated result substitutes for empirical human evidence.
evidence_sources.cost_access: Open teaching materials free; software and compute may be required.

free_task_specific_learning_resources.title: Creating Your First Model
free_task_specific_learning_resources.locator: Step-by-step Boltzmann wealth model notebook; introduces agent/model structure, steps and adding data collection and visualization.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.what_supported: Free hands-on ABM implementation lesson with explicit model rules and recorded outputs.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.limitations: A simple illustrative model only; learner must justify mechanism, inspect sensitivity and compare with relevant empirical evidence before drawing claims.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.cost_access: Free documentation and open-source framework; local Python setup or free third-party hosted notebook may be used. Hosted uptime is not guaranteed.

evidence_sources.title: Getting started
evidence_sources.locator: Framework overview and linked tutorials for first model, agent activation, scheduling, space, data collection and visualization.
evidence_sources.what_supported: Mesa is a documented agent-based modeling framework with an explicit beginner learning route.
evidence_sources.limitations: Framework availability does not validate a social model. Casevo is a separate emerging project and does not inherit Mesa's maintenance/resource status.
evidence_sources.cost_access: Mesa documentation and software are free/open source; Python compute required.

evidence_sources.title: Casevo: Cognitive Agents and Social Evolution Simulator
evidence_sources.locator: README: introduction, installation, basic tutorial and election-debate simulation; example implementation calls a separately configured Baichuan LLM API.
evidence_sources.what_supported: Establishes a real specialist project aimed at cognitive-agent/social-evolution simulation and a sample workflow.
evidence_sources.limitations: The checked sample needs an external LLM API key; no free-to-run end-to-end route was established. Current maintenance, reproducibility without paid API access and broad methodological validation are not established; do not recommend as a free learner path.
evidence_sources.cost_access: Repository and code viewable free; running the documented LLM-backed example may require a paid API account/credits. Exact provider terms can change.

free_task_specific_learning_resources.title: Creating Your First Model
free_task_specific_learning_resources.locator: Beginner notebook builds an agent model step by step; companion Getting Started page links scheduling, data collection and visualization tutorials.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.what_supported: Free runnable social-simulation framework instruction, suitable for the Mesa branch of this alternative-platform item.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.limitations: The example is a toy model, not an empirical claim or a validated account of human behavior. Does not teach Casevo or establish Casevo's API costs/maintenance as solved.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.cost_access: Free/open-source Mesa materials; Python environment and computer required. Cloud notebook option may have limits.

free_task_specific_learning_resources.title: Casevo: Cognitive Agents and Social Evolution Simulator — official repository tutorial
free_task_specific_learning_resources.locator: README sections 1–4.7: framework purpose, Mesa relationship, installation, election-debate simulation, model/agent construction and output analysis.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.what_supported: Official, task-specific learning route for constructing a cognitive-agent social simulation with Casevo; tutorial is free to read and source is open source.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.limitations: The documented runnable example calls Baichuan and requires an API key. Reproducing the full LLM-backed example may cost money and requires checking account eligibility, API compatibility and current model terms. It is an illustrative simulation, not evidence that simulated agents represent Nigerian people.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.cost_access: Free documentation and source; paid API usage may be required for the documented end-to-end example. See official Baichuan API/pricing route.

free_task_specific_learning_resources.title: Baichuan official API guide and pricing
free_task_specific_learning_resources.locator: API guide requires account real-name verification, top-up and API-key creation; current token-based charges: https://platform.baichuan-ai.com/prices.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.what_supported: Documented paid route for provisioning the LLM API dependency used by the Casevo example, subject to provider access and compatibility.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.limitations: Pricing, available models, account eligibility, regional access and Casevo compatibility can change. This is an API route, not a Casevo course or free-credit guarantee; learners should confirm current terms before spending.
free_task_specific_learning_resources.cost_access: Paid/token-metered API; consult official pricing page. No fixed total cost asserted because usage depends on prompts, outputs and model choice.

paid_or_official_routes.title: Baichuan official API guide and pricing
paid_or_official_routes.locator: API guide requires real-name verification, account top-up and API-key creation; current token-based charges are listed at https://platform.baichuan-ai.com/prices.
paid_or_official_routes.what_supported: Paid route for supplying the LLM API dependency in the official Casevo example, pending a hands-on compatibility check.
paid_or_official_routes.limitations: Not a free credit route or Casevo course. Price, provider access from Nigeria, available models and compatibility can change; confirm before paying.
paid_or_official_routes.cost_access: Paid/token-metered; no fixed total cost asserted.

paid_or_official_routes.title: Computer Simulations — Computational Social Science Specialization
paid_or_official_routes.locator: Course modules on agent-based models, Schelling’s segregation model, characteristics of ABM, and coding artificial societies in NetLogo; includes videos, readings and hands-on assignments.
paid_or_official_routes.what_supported: A university-taught, social-science-specific route to understand and design agent-based simulations that can prepare a learner for the modelling concepts underlying Casevo.
paid_or_official_routes.limitations: This teaches ABM and NetLogo, not Casevo. It does not establish that an LLM-agent simulation represents real people or validates a Nigerian social model. Coursera access, certificate and price depend on the learner’s region and current enrollment terms.
paid_or_official_routes.cost_access: Coursera lists enrollment options on the course page; certificate/graded access may require payment or subscription. Confirm current Nigeria availability and price before purchase; no fixed fee asserted.

unresolved.branch: Casevo as a freely reproducible learner route
unresolved.reason: An official Casevo tutorial and an official paid Baichuan API path are now documented. A free end-to-end Casevo run remains unverified; account availability from Nigeria, current model compatibility, pinned reproducibility and teaching-level maintenance still require a hands-on check. Keep Casevo optional with cost/availability disclosure; Mesa is the documented free runnable alternative.

evidence_sources.title: Working with text data
evidence_sources.locator: Tutorial steps: load text data, extract features, train a classifier, build a pipeline and evaluate performance.
evidence_sources.what_supported: Predictive text modeling is a specialist workflow requiring explicit features, a training task and evaluation.
evidence_sources.limitations: Technical scores do not validate the social construct, causal meaning, representativeness or transfer across populations/languages; human review and subgroup error analysis remain necessary.

evidence_sources.what_supported: Shows a real, bounded Nigerian-language text-classification task and annotated data route suitable for practicing sentiment classification; the paper reports task-specific evaluation rather than asserting universal language validity.

This does not resolve validation for an unspecified target construct/population. AfriSenti's sentiment labels cannot validate wellbeing, political attitudes or other constructs; for any chosen study, define the construct/population, confirm lawful data use, obtain suitable reference labels, check language/dialect coverage and report subgroup errors before making claims. Keep only the bounded sentiment exercise in scope; do not present generalized Nigerian social prediction as validated.
